newsitem.title: THAILAND: Real estate rescue plan sends Thai stocks higher.
newsitem.headline: Real estate rescue plan sends Thai stocks higher.

text.p: Foreign investors returned to Thailand's battered bourse on Tuesday, spurred by a government decision to launch a multi-billion dollar salvage operation for the real estate market.
The SET stock market index rose sharply on news that the cabinet had approved the plan, ending 16.63 points, or 2.36 percent, higher at 719.95.
The rise, the third in three straight sessions, helped erase most of the losses from last week's panic sell-off.

A government spokesman said the authorities would raise up to 100 billion baht ($3.87 billion) in seven-year, zero-coupon bonds to refinance property projects in distress and relieve a cash squeeze on their creditors.

The "property bond" is designed to turn around the fortunes of a market that has been in crisis for four years and bolster confidence in the country's finance companies, which have sunk a quarter of their lending into real estate.
Analysts gave the rescue plan a lukewarm welcome.

"I think 100 billion baht is enough money to help...but I don't know if it can solve the problems faced by buyers and developers," said Supon Pronchokchai, managing director of the Agency for Real Estate Affairs.
Warning that a support scheme for poor projects could prolong problems in the property sector, he said a far broader solution would be needed.
While the mood of panic over the health of the finance sector has dissipated, many investors still have doubts over slowing economic growth and faltering exports.
"The main figures to watch for now are January's economic figures," said Multi-Credit Corporation of Thailand president Surakiat Wongwasin, referring to trade and current account data.
"If they are not positive you could get another hiccup."
He said foreign speculators were still waiting in the wings to test the Bank of Thailand's resolve to defend the baht against devaluation.
Analysts said the central bank probably spent billions of dollars to fend off speculators between December and February.

The baht eased to 25.950-25.955 to the dollar from 25.937-25.942 on Monday following a comment from Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond that the currency would be made more flexible to counter speculative attacks.
Rerngchai gave no details of how and when the baht, which is pegged daily against a basket of currencies dominated by the dollar, would be given a freer rein.
Analysts believe the central bank may widen the dollar/baht trading band, fix its official pivot rate more than once a day or reduce the dollar's weighting in the basket.
The cabinet also approved a proposal on Tuesday to trim the 1996/97 (October/September) budget by 106 billion baht as part of a policy to rein in the current account deficit.
